Challenging judgment and award dated 12.07.2010 passed by Addl. Senior Civil Judge and Addl.
MACT, Haveri ('Tribunal' for short) in MVC no.193/2007, these appeals are filed.
2. MFA no.101982/2015 is filed by insurer challenging finding of Tribunal on liability, MFA 102541/2019 is filed by claimants for enhancement.
3. Sri Rajashekhar S. Arani, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal by insurer was on solitary ground.

It was submitted that there was no dispute about death of Hanumanthappa in accident that occurred on 07.01.2007 on Gudgeri - Samshi road involving insured tractor trailer unit The Divisional Manager vs Mallavva W/O. sentences.text: It was NC: 2026:KHC-D:4933 HC-KAR submitted that on account of death, while Smt.Mallava claiming to be wife of deceased Hanumantappa Ritti along with Kumari Suma, daughter had filed MVC no.193/2007 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Another claim petition came to be filed under provisions of Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 ('WC Act', for short) in WC no.91/2008.
Both petitions had proceeded parallelly and awards came to be passed.
Immediately on realizing that WC no.91/2008 was duplication of claim, appellant had filed Miscellaneous Petition no.14/2010 before Tribunal.
However, said Miscellaneous Petition came to be dismissed.
Therefore, insurer had challenged award.
4. On other hand, Sri BM Patil, learned counsel for claimants while opposing insurer's appeal submitted that claimants' appeal was for enhancement.

It was submitted, as on date of accident,
deceased Hanumantappa was aged 30 years and earning 9,000/- per month working as coolie.
However, Tribunal considered his monthly income as 3,000/- and awarded inadequate compensation.
It was submitted, claimants were wife and daughter.
Tribunal failed to add future prospects to monthly income and award adequate NC: 2026:KHC-D:4933 HC-KAR compensation under conventional heads.

On said ground sought for enhancement.
5. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment, award and record.

6. From above points that arise for consideration are:
1. Whether Tribunal was justified in holding insurer liable to pay compensation? and 2. Whether claimants were entitled for enhancement of compensation?
7.
Point no.1: Insurer's challenge is on sole ground that on same cause of action, another claim petition came to be filed under provisions of WC Act and award obtained.

To a query whether said claim was by claimants herein, learned counsel submitted that it was by Smt.Geeta claiming to be wife of Hanumantappa Ritti along with children giving an indication that deceased had two wives.

Unfortunately, though insurer claims to have filed miscellaneous petition before Tribunal to bring to its notice about duplication of claim, there is no effort on part of insurer either to produce award passed in WC or implead claimants therein as parties to address issue of NC: 2026:KHC-D:4933 HC-KAR duplication of claim or about entitlement.
For no other ground than this default, insurer's appeal requires to be dismissed.
Point no.1 is answered in 'affirmative'.
8. Point no.2:

Though claimants stated that deceased was working as coolie and earning 9,000/-
per month, same is not substantiated.
In absence, Tribunal assessed notionally.
Notional income for year 2007 is 4,000/-.
Therefore, Tribunal was not justified in taking it at 3,000/-.

As per decision in National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680,
in case of self- employed person aged below 40 years, 40% has to be added towards future prospects.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Deduction towards personal expenses has to be at 1/3rd and multiplier applicable would be '17'.

Consequently, compensation towards loss of dependency would be 7,61,532/- (4,000 +
40% - 1/3rd x 12 x 17).

sentences.text: In addition, claimant no.1 would be entitled for compensation towards loss of spousal consortium at 40,000/- and claimant no.2 for 40,000/- towards loss of filial consortium apart from 15,000/- towards loss of estate and 15,000/- towards funeral expenses.

Since more than 6 NC:
2026:KHC-D:4933 HC-KAR years have lapsed, claimants would be entitled for addition of 20% to award under conventional heads i.e. 22,000/-.
Thus, claimants would be entitled reassessed compensation at 8,93,532/-.
Point no.2 is answered 'partly in affirmative' as above.

Consequently,
following:
ORDER i. MFA no.102541/2019 is allowed in part.

ii. Claimants are held entitled for enhanced compensation of 8,93,532/- as against 4,48,000/- awarded by Tribunal with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit excluding 3186 days delay in filing appeal.
iii. Insurer is directed to deposit enhanced compensation within six weeks.
iv. On deposit, directions issued by Tribunal  towards apportionment of deposit and  release shall apply to enhanced  compensation proportionately.
v. MFA no.101982/2015 is dismissed.
vi. Amount in deposit, if any is ordered to be transmitted to Tribunal for payment.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:4933 HC-KAR vii.
Balance to be deposited before Tribunal within six weeks.
